title: Phase 1: zod for runtime schema validation
decision: Use zod for ingredient JSON runtime validation in Phase 1. Chosen over ajv (heavier) and hand-rolled validation (error-prone). zod's .enum() guards map cleanly to the controlled vocabulary union types already defined in TypeScript.
rationale: zod is already idiomatic in Vite/React stacks, produces typed parse results, and its enum guards directly enforce the controlled vocabulary invariants without a separate JSON schema file to maintain.

title: Phase 1: seed fixture must exercise all converter branches
decision: The Phase 1 seed fixture (10-15 ingredients) must include at least one example of: a pairsWith group ref, a pairsWith direct ID ref, a cuisineWeights object, a populated cookMinutes, and a blank cookMinutes. This ensures every converter branch is proven before Phase 2 runs the full 119-ingredient catalog.
rationale: If untested converter branches hit only in Phase 2, debugging cost multiplies. Testing all branches on a small hand-crafted fixture is cheap and prevents late surprises.

title: Vinegar group IDs: defer reconciliation to Phase 2
decision: Leave vinegar group as [red_wine_vinegar, sherry_vinegar, apple_cider_vinegar, white_wine_vinegar] until Phase 2 processes the full CSV catalog.
rationale: The architecture spec lists cider_vinegar but the likely actual catalog ID is apple_cider_vinegar (full name). white_wine_vinegar may also exist. Changing blindly risks Phase 2 group resolution failures. Phase 2 must verify these IDs match the catalog and update if needed.
revisit_if: Phase 2 processes the full CSV catalog and resolves actual ingredient IDs for vinegar items.

title: Build operations receive catalog as parameter
decision: buildReducer functions take catalog: Ingredient[] as a parameter for ID validation rather than importing the catalog module directly. This keeps build operations pure and independently testable without the real catalog.
rationale: Avoids implicit coupling to the static catalog import; lets tests inject small fixture catalogs. The React store layer passes the loaded catalog from context.

title: Skip: remove redundant assertValidStage runtime check in build.ts
decision: Leave the `assertValidStage` runtime guard in `updateBuildIngredient`. TypeScript already prevents invalid CookingStage values at compile time, so the check is dead code at runtime, but it costs nothing and guards against future JavaScript callers.
rationale: Removal adds noise to git blame for low signal; guard is harmless and adds belt-and-suspenders safety.
revisit_if: Next significant refactor of build.ts touches updateBuildIngredient.

title: Skip: unify deep-copy strategy between catalog.ts and store.tsx
decision: Leave `catalog.ts` using `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())` and `store.tsx` using `structuredClone`. Both are correct for the data shapes involved.
rationale: No behavioral difference for plain JSON-serializable ingredient/build data. Standardizing is churn; both approaches are defensible. Unify opportunistically when one file is next edited significantly.
revisit_if: Either file is substantially refactored, or a data type is introduced that JSON-roundtripping would corrupt (e.g. Date, undefined values).

title: Composer layout: four equal columns, vertical timeline
decision: The composer is four equal-width columns in order Library -> Detail -> Timeline -> Analysis; the cooking timeline is a vertical list of the 8 stages in canonical order (not a horizontal board), stacking to a single column on mobile.
rationale: A browse -> inspect -> place -> assess flow gives each step its own column; a vertical timeline reads naturally and reuses the same layout on mobile.
revisit_if: The timeline needs simultaneous cross-stage comparison better served by a horizontal board.

title: Placement model: select-to-detail then pick-stage; click+keyboard, no drag in MVP
decision: Placement is select-then-place: click a library ingredient to load Detail, then pick a target stage (default suggested) to send it to the timeline; every place/move/remove is click- and keyboard-operable, with drag-and-drop deferred as a later enhancement.
rationale: Guarantees the accessible non-drag path required by the drag-and-drop escalation trigger, and fully specifies the interaction for Phase 3 before any drag library is chosen.
revisit_if: Usability testing shows select-then-place is too slow and drag becomes the primary interaction (drag must still keep a keyboard/click equivalent).

title: Card face vs detail split
decision: Library card faces stay compact (name plus a salt-risk flag); full metadata, including balance-axis bars, is shown only in the Detail column.
rationale: Balance sparklines on the card face read as cryptic in the spike; a dedicated Detail column presents the ~12 ingredient fields legibly without crowding the browse list.
revisit_if: Users need at-a-glance balance while browsing without opening Detail.

title: Analysis column is a placeholder in Phase 3
decision: Phase 3 renders only a static summary (ingredient count, populated stage count, Phase 4 note) in the Analysis column. No balance bars, cuisine scores, or warnings are computed.
rationale: Analysis logic is Phase 4. Building the composer interaction model first keeps the two concerns independent and avoids wiring incomplete analysis into Phase 3 component tests.

title: Acceptance test fixes: salt-risk regex and remove-button focus (step 3.2 human steer)
decision: Two acceptance test assertions changed from frozen TESTS commit: (1) salt-risk queryByText(/low|medium|high/i) changed to getByText(/^(low|medium|high)$/i) to avoid matching heading text; (2) 30-iteration Tab scan for timeline remove button replaced with direct getByRole+focus() call.
rationale: Both changes were explicitly authorized by human steer in devlog entry '3.2 execute → partial'. The original assertions were buggy oracles: the regex matched content outside the salt-risk field, and the Tab scan was non-deterministic in jsdom. Both replacements are stricter or equally accurate tests of the same contract properties.
revisit_if: Never — both changes improve test fidelity without weakening the contract oracle.

title: Acceptance test query robustness: queryByText → queryAllByText for multi-match patterns
decision: Multiple acceptance test assertions changed from queryByText/getByText (throws on multiple matches) to queryAllByText/getAllByText[0] (safe with multiple matches). Affected: test_library lines 67/81/106/142; test_keyboard_a11y all inline getByText(/chicken/i) and queryByText(/chicken/i) calls; test_detail_and_placement lines 87/121/139/287/291; test_timeline_and_mutations lines 43/132.
rationale: Must fix: removing the getDisplayIngredients first-word deduplication (correct behavior — library must show all catalog members) caused all tests using single-match queries on 'chicken' or 'protein' to throw 'Found multiple elements'. The tests were written assuming deduplication; once deduplication was correctly removed, the queries needed to tolerate multiple results. The Should fix (showing actual role names instead of 'X roles listed') additionally caused 'protein' and 'body' to appear in both the category/roles field and the balance-axis label, also requiring the multi-match switch.
revisit_if: Tests are now robust to catalog size and deduplication changes. Only revisit if ingredient naming changes make the test search terms ambiguous.

title: Skip: simplify placeIngredient in App.tsx (remove redundant catalog.find)
decision: Leave the catalogIngredient lookup in App.tsx placeIngredient; the lookup is used only to check whether the chosen stage differs from the ingredient's catalog default before calling moveIngredient.
rationale: The defensive lookup avoids a no-op moveIngredient call when the user picks the default stage. Removing it would unconditionally call moveIngredient after insertIngredient, which works but produces an extra state update. Low value change; wait until placeIngredient gains broader editing logic.
revisit_if: placeIngredient is extended (e.g., stage validation, quantity prompts), at which point the whole function should be reviewed.

title: Analysis result types added to types.ts; thresholds are provisional
decision: Add AnalysisResult, AnalysisMessage, TimingFinding, IngredientSuggestion to types.ts. Composition warning thresholds (richness>=4, freshness<2, root count>=2) are provisional per ARCHITECTURE.md §Provisional Contracts; tune in Phase 4 step 8 against fixture builds before closing the phase.
rationale: Types belong alongside the other core data types; keeping them in types.ts avoids a circular import between analysis.ts and any future consumer.

title: Analysis engine is a pure module with no React/UI imports
decision: src/analysis.ts exports only analyzeBuild(build: StewBuild, catalog: Ingredient[]): AnalysisResult. No React, no store imports. The UI layer calls it and passes the result as props.
rationale: Keeps the function independently testable without a DOM environment. Follows the existing pattern of build.ts and catalog.ts being pure modules.

title: Fixture builds as typed TS constants in tests/fixtures/builds.ts
decision: Representative builds live in tests/fixtures/builds.ts as exported StewBuild constants. Each fixture is accompanied by an expectedAnalysis object documenting what analyzeBuild should return. Integration tests import both and assert.
rationale: Typed fixtures catch catalog drift (ingredient ID renames break the import). Colocating expected output with the fixture makes fixture intent self-documenting for future tuning.

title: Skip: inline formatCount helper in AnalysisPanel
decision: Leave formatCount as a named helper in AnalysisPanel.tsx.
rationale: Single call site; extracting to a helper adds no abstraction value. Could be inlined, but the helper has no cost and reads clearly.
revisit_if: A second call site appears or the component is significantly restructured.

title: Phase 5 step decomposition: instructions first, then persistence, then UI
decision: Steps proceed from pure logic outward to UI: (1) instruction generator, (2) persistence adapter — both pure/testable modules first; (3) pressure/release controls — small UI addition; (4) instructions panel — rendering of step 1; (5) saved builds UI — rendering of step 2; (6) E2E test closes the phase. Each step is independently verifiable before the next builds on it.
rationale: Pure-logic-first order lets TESTS author an acceptance suite against stable contracts before any UI exists; UI steps compose on a proven foundation.
